subject: Fresh independent security review (ADR-026 clause 5 / ADR-020 clause 8) of the amended ArrTags plugin log path: the bounded log subject (task 15.1, src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs), its threading through the ADR-026 clause 3 call sites (task 15.2), the bounded render classification (task 15.3), the IArrTagsLog<T>/ILogVerbosityGate/LogThrottle facade, the LogSubjectTests (23 cases) and LogRedactionTests (167 cases), and the canonical documentation changed for the amendment (ADR-020, ADR-026, architecture 06/12, README, docs/limitations). Attempt 2: the attempt-1 report at docs/implementation/15.4/security-review.json (written 2026-09-25 19:44 UTC by the previously launched security-reviewer CLI run) is preserved and was not overwritten; the delegation brief predated its completion and stated no prior report existed, so the contract attempt rule was followed.

findings.area: boundedness/log-integrity (required adjudication 1, Unicode Cf; TQ-15.1-2; corresponds to attempt-1 SR-15.4-01)
findings.description: ADJUDICATED ACCEPTABLE - no change required. LogSubject.NormalizeFileName removes only Unicode Cc scalars (Rune.IsControl). Cf format scalars and the Zl/Zp separators pass through verbatim: I reproduced U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE, U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE, U+200E LRM, U+061C ALM, U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR, and U+2029 PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR in the subject, and I reproduced a hostile subject emitted unchanged through the shipped ArrTagsLog<T> facade at Information and Trace (0 records at Warning). This matches clause 2's literal wording: 'control characters' names the Unicode Control category (Cc), Rune.IsControl matches exactly that category, and clause 2 says the name is 'otherwise emitted verbatim', so stripping Cf/Zl/Zp would exceed the clause rather than satisfy it. The residual is a log-display integrity weakness (bidi reordering, apparent line breaks in some viewers) available only to an actor who can name media files on the host; it is not a secret exposure (the value is still a file-name component or a D-format Guid), remains bounded at 128 scalars, and cannot evade the volume bound because LogThrottle admission keys on category|event only (reproduced: 1 tracked key). The current tree records the Cc-only decision in ADR-026's implementation note; no test pins the behavior in either direction.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs:84-99 (Rune.IsControl skip at :86; 128-scalar bound at :91-94)

/tmp/final-review/security/probe-output-a2.txt: probe 1 shows Cf/Zl/Zp pass-through (cats=Format/LineSeparator/ParagraphSeparator) while C0/C1 (U+0000, U+0001, CR, LF, tab, U+0085, U+007F) are removed; probe 2 shows Warning=0 records, Information=Trace=1 identical record with U+202E and U+2028 preserved

findings.recommended_action: No change required for this release; the Cc-only decision is now recorded. Optional future hardening (non-blocking): strip Cc+Cf+Zl+Zp (or at least U+2028, U+2029, U+202E) in NormalizeFileName and pin it with tests.

findings.area: redaction/host-path semantics (required adjudication 2; TQ-15.1-1 / 15.1-F1; corresponds to attempt-1 SR-15.4-02)
findings.description: For host-native paths, clause 1 holds. On the pinned Linux host every POSIX path shape I probed yields only the final component (absolute, nested with spaces, relative, '//server/share/file.mkv'), and trailing-separator/separator-only/root values fall back to the D-format item id; no separator can survive inside a POSIX component, so no directory, drive, share, or parent path is emitted. A Windows-style backslash string on Linux is one file name and is emitted whole (reproduced: C:\dir\share\file.mkv and \\server\share\file.mkv); that value is not a host-native path and cannot come from a real Linux media path (provenance: PrimaryPath is copied only by MediaIdentityFactory from MediaSourceInfo.Path/item.Path). The current tree scopes the documented claim correctly: ADR-020 amendment note, ADR-026 implementation note, architecture 06 (now host-native-path scoped), architecture 12 ('on the pinned Linux host ... a Windows-style backslash string is a single file name rather than a path'), the README LogVerbosity row (updated after attempt 1 to say 'of a host-native media path ... for a host-native media path it never writes a directory, share, or full path'), and the PLANS v1.2 risk row. Attempt-1's documentation recommendation is therefore applied in the tree; the code needs no change. Residual (non-actionable): a misconfigured non-host-native path value would be emitted as a filename-shaped string; it contains no credential, is bounded to 128 scalars, and is the host's own metadata.

findings.description: Documentation-wording issue, not a security issue. ADR-026 clause 3's mixed-site parenthetical lists the ineligible and connection-unavailable pre-publish discards as no-identity sites, but in the code both are reached after MediaIdentityFactory.TryCreate succeeded, where identity.MediaLocation.PrimaryPath can be available; the implementation follows the clause-3 enumeration and calls the 2-argument Discard, so those records take the item-identifier fallback. The fallback discloses strictly less than the file name (an opaque Guid, never a path), and no redaction, boundedness, or secret-freedom property depends on which subject is chosen; the changed-basis discards (configuration changed, item removed, item changed, no longer eligible, connection changed) do thread identity.MediaLocation?.PrimaryPath. The ADR-026 implementation note records the discrepancy without rewriting the clause, which is the correct handling for a decided ADR. No code change required.

findings.description: Confirmed secret-free and bounded. ArtworkGenerationResult.PassThroughReason, FailureReason, and SourceFailureReason are nullable members of the code-owned enums RenderPassThroughReason, RenderFailureReason, and ArtworkSourceReadFailureReason; the private constructor and the factories set at most one per result, and DescribeClassification interpolates it once by enum name. No exception message, reader/renderer detail, provider payload, path, or credential is reachable: the source-unavailable path substitutes a bounded reason string and never propagates the reader's text. The single artwork Information record measured 166 Unicode scalars in my facade probe with the hostile subject; the fixed text plus at most one bounded enum name cannot carry unbounded data. LogRedactionTests injects a raw reader-detail sentinel and asserts it never reaches a captured record.

findings.description: The canonical limitations register was not reconciled with the amendment. docs/limitations/accepted.md SEC-5 still presents the pre-ADR-026 allowlist as exhaustive ('Every log call emits only bounded, already-redacted values per the ADR-020 clause 4 allowlist (ArrProviderError code/retryability/message, the non-secret connection identity, configuration version, bounded reason codes and enums, item/record identifiers, and counts)'), and docs/data-model/03-12-configuration.md points readers at SEC-5 for the logging contract. The ADR-026 bounded log subject and the explicit directory/drive/share/full-path exclusion are missing from that enumeration. This does not overstate the security conclusion (the 'cannot leak a secret' sentence remains true, and no path/secret is incorrectly claimed absent), but a current-state register that enumerates the allowed log values is now incomplete for the amended contract; the task-15.4 documentation reconciliation covered only open.md, archive.md, and 00-index.md. The fix is one paragraph and is non-blocking for the review outcome.

findings.description: Path.GetFileName is a component splitter, not a file-type or URI parser, and two reproduced shapes are worth recording. (a) When MediaLocationSummary.PrimaryPath falls back to item.Path for an item with no media-source path and that value names a directory, the emitted subject is the item's final path component, i.e. a directory name (probe: '/media/movies/Some Movie Folder' -> 'Some Movie Folder'; '/mnt/nfs-share' -> 'nfs-share'). (b) A URL-shaped value is reduced to its last segment including any query string (probe: 'http://host/api/v3/movie?apikey=X' -> 'movie?apikey=X'), and authority userinfo is dropped as a side effect. Neither reaches the log in the shipped configuration: the sole producer of PrimaryPath is MediaIdentityFactory, which copies the Jellyfin host's MediaSourceInfo.Path/item.Path, and no provider payload, request URL, or PluginConfiguration field can reach the subject. Both shapes are bounded and credential-free, and shape (a) is a title-class value inside ADR-026's accepted disclosure trade-off (a media file/folder name may reveal a title), not directory structure.

findings.description: The redaction suite genuinely covers the amended sites. All eight boundaries and all ADR-026/classification theories run through the shipped facade (ArrTagsLog<T> + LogVerbosityGate + LogThrottle + host ILogger) with the seven sentinel values planted in the secret-bearing inputs; AssertNoSentinel scans every captured record at all six verbosity levels; and exact record counts prove level gating (0 records at Off/Error/Warning for the Information line). Each clause-3 site has a dedicated driver: the artwork coordinator (source-present, source-failure, and classification cases), both metadata-read-failure paths (a throwing Handler drives the catch, a failed Result drives the failed-read line), the mixed discard with and without a path, the pre-identity discard, both readers, worker processed and retry-scheduled, and lifecycle removal. The subject assertions pin the exact basename and forbid '/' in the record, so a directory or full-path leak fails. One optional strengthening: no call-site driver embeds a sentinel in a directory component of the path, so directory exclusion at the call sites rests on the '/' assertion plus the helper-level DirectorySegmentsNeverAppearInTheSubject; a directory-embedded sentinel would make the call-site claim direct.

summary: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS; no open BLOCKER or HIGH remains. The amended log path is secret-free, bounded, and redaction-enforced by shipped code rather than convention. Secret-freedom: I enumerated all 21 _log.Write call sites plus the facade's two writes; every interpolated value is a bounded enum, a Guid, a count, a code-owned literal, a 512-character-bounded ArrProviderError/WorkProcessingResult/ArtworkOperationErrors value, an exception type name, or the new bounded subject. No API key, webhook secret, SecretLease value, X-Api-Key/X-ArrTags-Webhook-Secret header, raw request/response body, full provider payload, or mutable PluginConfiguration can reach a record at any verbosity; the 167-case sentinel suite drives all eight boundaries at all six verbosity levels and passes (plus 23 LogSubject cases; full suite 0/1619/63/1682). Boundedness: the subject is at most 128 Unicode scalar values after control removal in a single scalar-wise pass that never splits a surrogate pair, the classification is a bounded enum name appended once (at most one), and 512-character bounds protect the pre-existing reason fields; the subject is deliberately not part of the LogThrottle key (reproduced: 1 tracked key for 40 hostile names), so a hostile file name cannot amplify or evade the clause 6 volume bound. Redaction: for host-native paths no directory, drive, share, or parent component is emitted, enforced by Path.GetFileName plus the bound and pinned by the helper tests and the per-site basename/no-slash assertions; the tree now states the host-native scope in ADR-020, ADR-026, architecture 06/12, README, and the PLANS risk row. Required adjudications: (1) Cf/Zl/Zp pass-through is acceptable under clause 2 as written (Cc is the Unicode Control category and the clause says otherwise-verbatim), recorded in ADR-026's implementation note, with optional non-blocking hardening (SR2-15.4-01); (2) clause 1 is satisfied for host-native paths and the documentation now scopes the claim (SR2-15.4-02, resolved); (3) IR-15.2-04 is a documentation-wording matter only, conservative fallback, recorded (SR2-15.4-03); (4) the classification qualifiers are bounded enums with no free text (SR2-15.4-04). One open LOW documentation finding remains: SEC-5 in docs/limitations/accepted.md still enumerates the pre-ADR-026 allowlist and points at the amended clause 4 (SR2-15.4-05); it does not overstate the security conclusion and does not block, but it should be reconciled in the same register. Attempt-1 (docs/implementation/15.4/security-review.json) is preserved; this attempt-2 report is the fresh independent review, and its one open LOW changes no BLOCKER/HIGH status.
